name: The Bright Accounting: Fifty Years of the Sable Charter
description: Commissioned jointly by the Sable Charter Governance Consortium to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Charter's ratification, this high-production neural-feed documentary presents half a century of corponation self-governance as an unambiguous success story measured in infrastructure indices, life expectancy averages, and economic productivity metrics — all of which are technically accurate and all of which exclude Tier 1 populations from their sample bases. The film's immersive neural format allows viewers to experience reconstructed versions of pre-Charter urban decay, making the contrast with present-day Tier 3-4 prosperity viscerally compelling in a way that is extraordinarily difficult to critically analyze while experiencing it.
cultural_impact: The film's neural-feed experience of pre-Charter 'collapse conditions' became so culturally embedded that it is now routinely cited by Tier 3 residents in political conversations as personal memory rather than produced content, representing what media critics call the most successful instance of manufactured historical consensus in GLMZ's documentary history.
story_hooks: A player character experiences an inconsistency in the neural reconstruction — a building or face that doesn't match the historical period depicted — suggesting the 'documentary' footage contains fabricated elements the production team may not have been fully aware of.
The statistical analysts who published the counter-narrative are being systematically pressured, and one of them has gone quiet in a way that worries their colleagues.
A senior producer on the documentary left the project eight months before completion under circumstances that were officially described as 'creative differences' and has not spoken publicly since.
